summary: Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Shechen Gyaltsab and Khenpo Shenga.
Pema Tsering worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Shenga, held a post at the University of Bonn attested in 1996, and taught Ruth Gamble.
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga. He also taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khakyab Dorje, and Khenpo Shenga. He taught Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Khenpo Shenga.

Penghao Sun works in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, Qingying Chen (2009–2011), Weirong Shen, Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Peter K. Bol, Jay Jasanoff, James Robson, Ryuichi Abe, and Jie Li.
Penor 02 both studied under and taught Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Palyul Monastery under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Dilgo Khyentse, Jampel Gyepai Dorje, and Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, and founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978.

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1935–1949) under Gustaf John Ramstedt (~1935–1939). He served as Docent of Comparative Linguistics at the University of Helsinki from 1958 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) studied Tibetology at the University of Copenhagen under Erik Haarh. He lectured at Copenhagen (1982–1989), researched at the University of Bonn (1991–1992), and served as a professor at Leipzig University from 1994 to 2017.

Per Kværne (born 1945) works in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Oslo, he lectured at the University of Bergen (1970–1975) and served as a professor at the University of Oslo from 1975 to 2007.
Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Rau (~1968–1971). He held a post at the University of Marburg from circa 1968 to 1991.
Perry Link (born 1944), a scholar of Sinology and linguistics, earned a B.A. at Harvard. He held posts at Princeton (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and UC Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) studied and habilitated at the University of Munich. He held posts at Munich, Innsbruck, Salzburg, the University of Glasgow (2000–2009), and the University of Münster (2009–2023) in religious studies, theology, and philosophy.

Peter Adamson (born 1972) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Williams College and the University of Notre Dame. He held posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).
Peter Alan Roberts works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed his doctoral studies under Michael Aris.

Peter Bisschop earned his PhD at the University of Groningen under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He was a fellow at Wolfson College, Oxford, lectured at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010), and held an editorial post at Leiden University (attested 2011–2021).

Peter Connolly works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and became a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock (born 1958) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University and under Seungsahn Haengwon and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, serving as Director of the East-West Center's Asian Studies Development Program (attested 2007–2013).
Peter Ebbatson is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.
Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and advisers N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, and held a post at Deakin University.
